static int qmi_wwan_probe(struct usb_interface *intf,
			  const struct usb_device_id *prod)
{
	struct usb_device_id *id = (struct usb_device_id *)prod;
	struct usb_interface_descriptor *desc = &intf->cur_altsetting->desc;

	/* Workaround to enable dynamic IDs.  This disables usbnet
	 * blacklisting functionality.  Which, if required, can be
	 * reimplemented here by using a magic "blacklist" value
	 * instead of 0 in the static device id table
	 */
	if (!id->driver_info) {
		dev_dbg(&intf->dev, "setting defaults for dynamic device id\n");
		id->driver_info = (unsigned long)&qmi_wwan_info;
	}

	/* Quectel EC20 quirk where we've QMI on interface 4 instead of 0 */
	if (quectel_ec20_detected(intf) && desc->bInterfaceNumber == 0) {
		dev_dbg(&intf->dev, "Quectel EC20 quirk, skipping interface 0\n");
		return -ENODEV;
	}

	return usbnet_probe(intf, id);
}

static struct usb_driver qmi_wwan_driver = {
	.name		      = "qmi_wwan",
	.id_table	      = products,
	.probe		      = qmi_wwan_probe,
	.disconnect	      = usbnet_disconnect,
	.suspend	      = qmi_wwan_suspend,
	.resume		      =	qmi_wwan_resume,
	.reset_resume         = qmi_wwan_resume,
	.supports_autosuspend = 1,
	.disable_hub_initiated_lpm = 1,
};

module_usb_driver(qmi_wwan_driver);

Confirmed: qmi_wwan in s10 is the same vintage as s08. In s08 the finding was at line 699 in a differently-shaped qmi_wwan.c (bind at 744, register_subdriver at 686). In s10: bind at 348, register_subdriver at 290, endpoint[0] at 304, usb_cdc_wdm_register at ~313.

Note difference: in s10, the `if (info->control != info->data) dev->status = &info->control->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0];` is guarded by control != data. Then `if (!dev->status) rv = -EINVAL;` — so for the single-interface case, status remains NULL and subdriver registration fails → bind fails. So the NULL-deref path needs control != data with a zero-endpoint control interface. That's the same as the s08 reasoning (in s08 the same structure? In s08 finding: "info->control starts as the probed interface; a CDC Union descriptor's bSlaveInterface0 can move info->data to a different interface, leaving info->control == intf while info->data != info->control" — same structure).
